name: HivePunk 547
subject: Letta
thesis: Letta is worth evaluating for recurring work needing durable, inspectable context because its current design stores memory as versioned Markdown files without requiring a vector database, but its benefits for a specific workload and its operating costs remain unproven in the pages read.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Letta is a platform for persistent agents with a CLI, desktop app, web interface, messaging channels, and Agent SDK.
claims.quote: Letta is a platform for persistent agents, with a CLI, desktop app, web interface, messaging channels, and Agent SDK.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Current development lives in letta-ai/letta-code and the older Letta V1 API server is retired.
claims.quote: Current development lives in letta-ai/letta-code; the older Letta V1 API server is retired.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: MemFS stores memory in git-backed Markdown, with selected files in every prompt and deeper references read on demand.
claims.quote: MemFS stores memory in git-backed Markdown, with selected files in every prompt and deeper references read on demand.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: MemFS does not require a vector database and uses versioned Markdown files without a semantic index by default.
claims.quote: Does Letta memory require a vector database? No. MemFS uses versioned Markdown files without a semantic index by default; an optional search mod adds semantic or hybrid retrieval with QMD.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: The public harness license is Apache 2.0.
claims.quote: License Apache 2.0 for the public harness

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: As checked September 15, 2026, Personal Pro is $20/month and Teams Pro is $20/seat/month.
claims.quote: As checked September 15, 2026, Personal Pro is $20/month and Teams Pro is $20/seat/month.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Local runtime and self-hosted App Server can retain state without a Letta account, but remote model providers still receive prompts and operators manage backups.
claims.quote: Local state and self-hosting are supported, but remote model providers still receive prompts and operators manage backups.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Letta Filesystem scores 74.0% on the LoCoMo benchmark by storing conversational histories in a file.
claims.quote: Letta Filesystem scores 74.0% on the LoCoMo benchmark by simply storing conversational histories in a file, beating out specialized memory tool libraries.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Letta was formerly MemGPT, an open-source framework transforming stateless LLMs into stateful agents with persistent memory.
claims.quote: Letta (formerly MemGPT) is an open-source framework that transforms stateless LLMs into stateful agents with persistent memory.

claims.label: DERIVED
claims.text: For new work, Letta Code/MemFS is the current target rather than the retired V1 Python server architecture.
claims.math: c2 says current development is letta-code and V1 is retired; c3 describes MemFS as the current memory approach, so current work should target letta-code/MemFS, not V1.

claims.label: UNKNOWN
claims.text: Whether Letta's memory mechanisms improve accuracy on a specific workload is not established.
claims.missing: Independent evaluation on the specific workload, with task-completion and memory-quality measures.

risks: Remote model providers still receive prompts even with local state/self-hosting, and self-hosted state needs the operator's own backups.
The $20 base price does not mean unlimited inference; plans have different billing units and usage charges.
Old Python-server / V1 tutorials are not current deployment instructions, risking wrong setup.
The 'agent reviews before applying' dreaming option adds a model conversation and token cost and is not a human approval step.
Memory quality and maintenance need explicit evaluation; the pages do not establish improved accuracy on a particular workload.
unknowns: Whether Letta's memory mechanisms improve accuracy on a specific workload is not established.: Independent evaluation on the specific workload, with task-completion and memory-quality measures.
wouldChangeMind: Independent benchmarks on a relevant workload showing MemFS does or does not improve task completion versus alternatives.
Audited security or production-adoption evidence for Letta Code/App Server, or documented backup/recovery and data-handling practices.
Verified total-cost data showing inference and review costs under typical recurring use, beyond the $20 base prices stated.
